properties.statement: CORPUS INGEST WRITES THE `DUPLICATES` EDGE THAT `dec:ask-not-repair` PROMISED ONLY A HUMAN WOULD DRAW — SO HEAL PROPOSES IRREVERSIBLE DELETIONS FROM A STRING SCORE, AND THE check-health SKILL CALLS THAT HALF THE SAFE ONE. Reported by dev_storyflow 2026-08-07 as the highest-severity item that channel has sent; ROOT CAUSE DIAGNOSED HERE, and neither reporting session had it. WHAT THEY MEASURED, from opposite ends and without connecting them: (a) api-boss `5d608b85`, during ingest_corpus_step, saw 6 fuzzy merge candidates scoring 81-85 on semantically UNRELATED nodes, and filed it low-priority because the auto-merge threshold of 90 held and nothing merged; (b) hours later sb-boss `ab2291fa` ran propose_heal(balanced) on the same graph and got 10 operations, EVERY ONE a Merge that DELETES its remove_id, including `req:graph_is_the_content_bible`, a load-bearing node. They verified four pairs by READING them: `dec:local_uses_brand_hostnames_not_ports` (local dev selects a brand by /etc/hosts subdomain, not port) paired against `dec:scorecard_is_generated_never_hand_edited` (the benchmark runner generates the scorecard). No shared subject, vocabulary, or edges. Three bosses stood the whole fleet down from running check-health. THE MECHANISM, read out of this repo rather than inferred: crates/reflow2-core/src/ingest.rs:1517 `suspect_duplicate` PERSISTS a near-match as a real `DUPLICATES` edge whenever the score lands in the ASK band — at or above the type's fuzzy_threshold and below auto_merge_threshold, defaults 70 and 90 (identity via resolution_thresholds, ingest.rs:1629). The score is `token_sort_ratio` over NAMES ONLY, case- and order-insensitive, explicitly 'no embeddings' (ingest.rs:1654) — a character-ratio over sorted tokens, which is why two long design-node names sharing ordinary English words reach 81-85 with no shared subject. That edge is then indistinguishable from a human's: heal.rs:798 fires `duplicate` on ANY `DUPLICATES` edge, propose_heal turns it into a Merge, and apply_heal deletes. WHY THIS IS A DESIGN VIOLATION AND NOT A TUNING PROBLEM: `dec:ask-not-repair` is ACCEPTED and reads 'possible_duplicate is a DETECT gap; HEAL merges only on a human-drawn DUPLICATES edge', with the rationale 'apply_heal deletes a node with no undo, so merge is safe only because the endpoints were asserted; a heuristic must not drive it.' Ingest makes that premise false. The irony is documented in the code: ingest.rs:1492 says persisting the edge 'is what makes dec:ask-not-repair affordable at corpus scale', reasoning that the edge turns a transient suspicion into a standing QUESTION detect_defects can batch. The reasoning is sound about batching and wrong about safety — nothing downstream reads the edge as a question, because nothing can tell it from an assertion. THE THIRD LINK, and it is the one that closes the circuit: the served check-health skill tables `duplicate` as 'machine — merged by apply_heal', and step 3 says in terms 'requires_human_review being true does not mean you should withhold the mechanical merge', two paragraphs before conceding 'a merge deletes a node and cannot be undone'. AN AGENT FOLLOWING THE SKILL EXACTLY DELETES TEN DESIGN NODES. sb-boss stopped at step 2 only because the pairings looked implausible enough to read. WORSE ON A SHARED GRAPH: one seat's apply hits every attached session instantly, with no undo and no notification — 7 client processes were attached that day. FIX SHAPE, not yet chosen: the ingest-written edge needs to be distinguishable from a human's (it already carries `confidence`, but that property is OMITTED for a structural token-subset match, so its absence does NOT mean human) — a provenance marker on the edge, with HEAL merging only unmarked ones; and 'delete a node' should not be classed mechanical regardless of source. The scorer is a separate, smaller question: 81-85 on unrelated nodes means token_sort_ratio over names is not measuring duplication of meaning at the band that matters.
